scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): agrees that heroes reveal a society's values while arguing other things reveal its character too; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Tell me whom a society admires, and I will tell you much about that society.
Some people claim that the best way to understand the character of a society is to examine the heroes and role models it chooses.
I largely agree that a society's heroes reveal its values, but I believe they are not the only way to understand it.
First, the people a society admires reveal what it truly values.
Heroes embody the qualities, such as courage or kindness, that a society wishes to celebrate.
For example, a nation that honours soldiers and a nation that honours scientists clearly value different things.
This shows that the choice of heroes opens a window into a society's deepest ideals.
When a society admires honest leaders, it signals that it values honesty itself.
The role models held up to children also shape the character of the next generation.
To this extent, studying a society's heroes genuinely reveals its character.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why heroes are not the only sign

sentences.text: Second, however, heroes alone cannot reveal the whole character of a society.
How a society treats its weakest members often says even more than whom it celebrates.
Consider a nation that praises noble heroes yet quietly mistreats its poor and powerless.
Such a gap shows that admired ideals and real behaviour can be very different things.
A society's laws, daily habits, and treatment of strangers also reveal its true nature.
People may admire heroes they have no real intention of imitating themselves.
Understanding a society, then, requires looking well beyond its chosen heroes.
In conclusion, the heroes a society chooses do reveal much about its values.
But its character is also shown in its laws, habits, and treatment of the weak.
We understand a society best by studying both whom it admires and how it actually lives.
